name: Virginia
keyNotes: Judicial sale process — court involvement required
Rural Southwest and Southside Virginia offer best investor opportunity
Northern Virginia (NoVA) has essentially no accessible inventory — prices too high for tax deed plays
summary: Virginia requires 3 years of delinquency before a judicial sale with oral upset bids. Each locality (city or county) manages independently — no statewide calendar. Northern Virginia has strong high-value inventory. Statute: VA Code §58.1-3965.
typeWhy: Virginia sells the property deed outright through judicial sale after 3 years of tax delinquency. There is no post-sale redemption period. VA Code §58.1-3965.
rateWhy: Virginia is a deed state with no statutory interest rate. Auction prices are market-driven through oral upset bidding in judicial sale proceedings. VA Code §58.1-3965.
notBeginnerReason: 3-year delinquency required, judicial sale process, each locality manages independently — slow and complex.
beginnerTip: Focus on localities with consistent judicial sale schedules — Prince William, Henrico, and Chesterfield have regular activity. Budget for attorney costs upfront.
risks: 3-year delinquency must be verified before pursuing
Judicial sale process adds attorney costs and time
Each locality manages independently — no unified schedule
ddExtra: Verify the 3-year delinquency threshold has been met
Hire a Virginia-licensed attorney familiar with judicial tax sales
Confirm no IRS or federal liens — these survive Virginia tax sales

steps: Identify your target locality at virginia.gov/agencies/local-government
Contact the local treasurer or circuit court — ask when the next judicial sale is scheduled
Hire a local Virginia attorney for the judicial sale process — highly recommended
Register per the court's instructions and attend in person
auctionSignup.depositInfo: Varies by locality. Attorney costs add $1,500–$3,500.

tylerCompliance.summary: Virginia updated Code to mandate surplus return from delinquent tax sales.
tylerCompliance.details: Virginia 2024 amendment to Code §58.1-3967 requires that surplus proceeds from delinquent real estate tax sales be paid to the former owner after satisfaction of all liens and costs. The treasurer must provide notice by certified mail within 30 days of sale. Unclaimed surplus is held for 3 years before escheating to the Literary Fund.

process.eligibility: Standard: delinquent on Dec 31 following the 2nd anniversary of due date. Accelerated (1 yr): assessed value ≤$100K OR condemned, blighted, nuisance, or derelict structure.
process.attorney: Treasurer refers property to delinquent tax attorney or TACS (Tax Administration Collection Services)
process.courtFiling: Attorney files suit in Circuit Court against the property
process.specialCommissioner: Court appoints a Special Commissioner of Sale to conduct auction, private bid, or list with agent
process.preAuction: Owner may redeem at any time before sale date by paying all taxes + penalties + interest + costs + attorney fees (VA Code §58.1-3974)
process.saleMethod: Special Commissioner may use: (1) public auction, (2) private bid/offer, or (3) real estate agent listing — at commissioner's discretion
process.courtApproval: Court must confirm sale. Process typically takes 1–18 months total.
process.deed: Special Warranty Deed from Special Commissioner — conveyed free and clear of all liens

auction.platform: TACS (taxva.com) / Woltz & Associates / courthouse auction / online — varies by locality
auction.bidMethod: Highest bidder — public auction OR private offer process
auction.deposit: Typically 10% of purchase price or $1,000 minimum — cashier's check
auction.minimumBid: Generally must bear relation to property value — court may reject unreasonably low bids
auction.noLienCerts: CRITICAL: Virginia does NOT sell tax lien certificates. No OTC lien purchases. Judicial sale ONLY.

otc.name: N/A — Virginia has no OTC or lien cert sales
otc.note: After court confirmation, deed issued. If property doesn't sell, may be listed again or sold via private bid.

subTax.name: N/A — Virginia is deed/judicial sale state, no lien cert sub-tax

redemption.period: Until day before sale (up to 5pm day prior per some localities)
redemption.postSale: NO post-sale redemption under Virginia law
redemption.statute: VA Code §58.1-3974, Roanoke County FAQ confirmed
redemption.note: Owner MUST redeem before gavel falls. Once court confirms sale — no recovery.

deedPath.name: Special Warranty Deed via Special Commissioner's Sale
deedPath.titleQuality: Free and clear of all liens — court ordered. Special warranty (not general warranty).

surplus.name: Surplus / Excess Proceeds
surplus.process: Special Commissioner reports to court with accounting of all proceeds and disbursements. Surplus distributed by court order in priority. Former owner claims surplus via court proceeding.
surplus.note: Tyler v. Hennepin applies — VA judicial process already distributes surplus to prior owners via court.

keyProviders.tacs: TACS (Tax Administration Collection Services) — taxva.com — handles many VA localities
keyProviders.woltz: Woltz & Associates — woltz.com — conducts many SW Virginia judicial auctions

es.redemption: Ninguna (se requieren 3 años de morosidad antes de la venta)
es.summary: Virginia requiere 3 años de morosidad antes de una venta judicial con pujas orales de protesta. Cada localidad (ciudad o condado) gestiona independientemente — sin calendario estatal. El norte de Virginia tiene inventario de alto valor fuerte. Estatuto: VA Code §58.1-3965.
es.typeWhy: Virginia es un estado de escritura porque las localidades venden propiedades embargadas a través de ventas judiciales, sin derecho de redención. Se requieren 3 años de morosidad (VA Code §58.1-3965).
es.rateWhy: No se aplica tasa de interés ya que es un estado de escritura judicial. Los costos de abogado ($1,500-$3,500) reducen el margen (VA Code §58.1-3965).
es.notBeginnerReason: Se requieren 3 años de morosidad, proceso de venta judicial, cada localidad gestiona independientemente — lento y complejo.
es.beginnerTip: Enfóquese en localidades con calendarios de venta judicial consistentes — Prince William, Henrico y Chesterfield tienen actividad regular. Presupueste los costos de abogado por adelantado.
risks: El umbral de morosidad de 3 años debe verificarse antes de proceder
El proceso de venta judicial agrega costos de abogado y tiempo
Cada localidad gestiona independientemente — sin calendario unificado
ddExtra: Verifique que se haya cumplido el umbral de morosidad de 3 años
Contrate un abogado con licencia de Virginia familiarizado con ventas fiscales judiciales
Confirme que no hay gravámenes del IRS o federales — estos sobreviven a las ventas fiscales de Virginia

auctionSignup.platform: Tribunal de Circuito o Tesorero (específico por localidad)
steps: Identifique su localidad objetivo en virginia.gov/agencies/local-government
Contacte al tesorero local o tribunal de circuito — pregunte cuándo es la próxima venta judicial
Contrate un abogado local de Virginia para el proceso de venta judicial — muy recomendado
Regístrese según las instrucciones del tribunal y asista en persona
auctionSignup.depositInfo: Varía por localidad. Los costos de abogado agregan $1,500–$3,500.
